item.description: - **Client certificates, as in Safari.** When a site asks for a certificate to identify you (a company intranet, a bank), Changmun offers the ones in your Keychain or on a smart card that the site accepts, in the system's own sheet. What you pick is saved as an identity preference for that site (remove it in Keychain Access), so the next visit doesn't ask. Private windows save nothing, and a page the AI is using always asks you: the AI never picks a certificate for you, not even one you chose before.

- **Rename bookmark folders.** Double-click a folder in the sidebar, pinned ones included, or choose Rename… from its menu. Only the name you see changes: the folder stays pinned or open, importing again from the same browser keeps your name, and clearing the name brings the original back. - **Typing Korean (or any input method) in the address bar.** Suggestions now follow what the field shows, the syllable still being composed included, so choosing the first row or pressing Return opens the whole of what you typed, not the part before the last syllable. - **Return opens the highlighted suggestion.** When results arrived after you started typing, Return could open a row from the earlier list instead. - **A click opens the suggestion it went down on,** even if the list changes under the pointer before the button comes up. - **A tab group's header answers a click anywhere along it;** a few narrow spots used to ignore single clicks, which also made double-click renaming unreliable.

- **Rename bookmarks and favorites.** Double-click a bookmark in the sidebar (pinned folders included) or choose Rename… from its menu; a favorite tile renames from its menu. The name is kept, even if you import from that browser again, and Undo brings the old one back. - **Rename a group with a double-click** on its header in the sidebar or its chip in the tab strip. - **A group chip being renamed in the tab strip** no longer hides the first letter behind its dot.

- **Tabs on top, if you like.** Settings › Appearance › Tab Layout now offers On Top: a tab strip above the address bar, with your favorites first as icon-only tiles, then the space's tabs, tab groups as a chip that collapses them, and a + button that stays in view when the tabs overflow. Middle-click closes a tab, dragging reorders, double-clicking renames, and the menus are the sidebar's. The rest of the sidebar opens over the page from the button beside the address bar. The sidebar layout is unchanged and still the default. - **Choose the model and how hard it thinks.** The menu under the AI message box picks the model and an effort level (Auto, Low, Medium, High, Extra High, Max), passed to Claude Code; Auto leaves it to Claude Code. - **Three approval modes.** Ask after reading other sites (the default, as before), Ask before every action (also before typing, choosing or clicking on a page when the chat has read nothing else), or Ask only for actions that can't be undone (the old "off"). Paying, sending, posting, deleting and the like, sign-ins and cookie banners are asked in every mode. Choose from the hand menu under the message box or in Settings › AI; your current setting carries over. - **A + menu and dictation in the message box.** Add Tab…, Attach Screenshot and Add Image… live in one menu, the mic starts macOS dictation, and Stop sits in the box (Esc still stops). - **The panel's head shows the chat.** Its title with a menu of recent chats and Show All Chats, a new-chat button, and a button that pops the panel out into its own window (closing it docks the panel back; the AI's questions come to that window). - **See what it's doing.** "Working for 12 s" with the live steps underneath, cards for the pages that went with your message, and a small ring showing how much of the model's context the chat uses. - **Double-clicking the bar zooms the window again,** following System Settings › Desktop & Dock › "Double-click a window's title bar to".

- **Rename a tab.** Double-click a tab's title in the sidebar, or choose Rename Tab… from its menu, and give it a name of your own. The name stays through new pages, restarts and reopening; Reset Name brings back the page's title. The AI still sees the page's real title next to your name. - **Imported folders keep one name.** Folders brought in from Chrome, Arc or Safari are stored under the same name whatever language your Mac is in, and shown in yours, so importing again after a language change no longer makes a second copy. Folders imported before are renamed once at launch, with a backup kept first, and folders imported twice in two languages are merged. - **Safari's favorites folder** no longer shows as "/ Favorites".

A sweep for bugs that hadn't bitten anyone yet, 47 of them. The ones you might have met:
- **Your newer passwords stay.** Importing again from another browser no longer puts its older passwords and sign-in cookies over the ones you changed in Changmun. Logins on different ports of one host stay apart, and a two-step sign-in updates your account instead of saving a nameless one. - **Nothing is wiped by a damaged file.** If chat history or archived tabs can't be read, the file is kept aside instead of being written over with an empty one. Saving a page with a long Korean title works, and downloading over an existing file keeps it until the new one is whole. - **Videos and pages stay put.** A paused picture-in-picture video is no longer put to sleep, a page in full screen can't be taken by the AI, a page whose process crashed on its first load loads again, and sign-in pop-ups from the preview card finish. - **Tabs where you left them.** Undoing "close all in group" or a tidy brings tabs back in order, a tab whose bookmark was deleted or moved to another space's favorites stays in the list, and private windows can't save to your bookmarks. - **Smoother start and quit.** Changmun no longer waits on the Safari extension list at launch, ends Claude Code before it quits, and won't wake a tab you closed while it was asking. - **Command line and agents.** `changmun` rejects arguments a command doesn't take, finds and restarts the app after a crash, and the MCP bridge keeps each connection's calls in order and answers pings right away. - **Ranges in AI answers read right.** "3~5" and "10~20" no longer turn the words between them into strikethrough; only ~~two tildes~~ strike through.

- **No more white page after full-screen video.** Leaving a video's full screen (YouTube's f key, for one) could leave the page blank and white until something else happened. Changmun redrew the tab while the video was full screen and lost the spot the page had to come back to. It now leaves the page alone during full screen and puts it back in place when you leave it.

- **Translation tries the other engine.** On some Macs, the translation engine macOS reports as ready refuses to translate. When one engine turns down the whole page, Changmun now tries the other one, then the system's default, before giving up. If macOS's translation doesn't respond at all, it says so and points to Translation Languages in System Settings. - **A record of why a translation failed.** Changmun notes in the system log which languages and engines it tried and what macOS answered, never the page's text or address. If a page still won't translate, run `log show --last 10m --style compact --predicate 'subsystem == "io.github.namekun.Changmun" AND category == "translation"'` in Terminal and send the output along with your report.

- **The loading bar keeps clear of the address.** It still touched letters like g and p at the bottom of the address bar. Loading now shows as a thin line along the top edge of the page, in every toolbar layout.

- **The loading bar sits on the address bar's edge.** It used to float just under the address text and touch letters like g and p. It now runs along the bottom edge of the address bar, rounded with it. - **The command bar and page previews open over the page.** They're centred on the page instead of the window, so they no longer cover the sidebar. - **Orange text you can read in light mode.** Errors, approval questions and "no results" use a darker orange in light mode. - **Small fixes.** The save-login bar shortens the user name before the site name, and the list in onboarding lines up with its buttons.
